Pool surround cleaning in Melbourne

The one surface where grip matters more than looks

Coping, paving, decking and travertine around a pool. It is the dampest hard surface on any property, so it grows the most, and it is the one surface people walk on wet with bare feet. Cleaning it is a safety job that happens to also make it look good.

  • Run off kept out of the pool
  • Anti slip sealing where it is warranted
  • Never acid on travertine or limestone
Get A Quote 0400 638 010
  1. Home
  2. Services
  3. Pressure and surface cleaning
  4. Pool surround cleaning

Why it goes first

Splash out, humidity, shade from the fence and whatever is planted around it keep a pool surround damp for most of the year. Algae needs exactly that, and wet algae on smooth stone has almost no grip at all.

The sequence is predictable. It goes slightly green in the shaded corner. It becomes slippery underfoot while still looking basically fine, which is the dangerous window. Then it looks obviously dirty, by which point it has been a hazard for a season. The useful time to clean a pool surround is when it starts feeling different underfoot rather than when it starts looking different.

By surround material

What it takes, and what grip it has wet

The common Melbourne pool surround materials, with the two things that matter.
  How it is cleaned Grip when wet
Travertine Low pressure, neutral chemistry. Never acid, which dissolves it Good unfilled, poor once the holes fill and polish
Bluestone Low to moderate, longer dwell, test patch Good sawn, poor honed. Porous so it stains as well
Exposed aggregate Moderate, pre-treated because growth sits between stones Very good. The most forgiving surround material
Concrete pavers Moderate, then joints re-sanded Good textured, moderate smooth
Stamped or stencilled concrete Low pressure only, usually a failing coating Poor once the coating is worn or if it was sealed gloss
Timber decking Low pressure, with the grain, then usually re-oiled Poor when wet and algal. The highest risk surround of all

Swipe for the rest of the columns

Keeping it out of the pool

What is not optional around a pool

Run off is directed away

Cleaning solution and everything that comes off the surround goes away from the waterline rather than into it. On a surround that falls toward the pool that means working in sections and managing the flow.

Chemistry chosen with the pool in mind

Products are selected so that incidental overspray does not create a water balance problem. It is why a pool surround is not quoted as just another slab.

Cover and skimmer check

Skimmer boxes and any cover are protected before we start, and the surface is rinsed thoroughly at the end so nothing is left to wash in with the next rain.

Tell us about the pool

Salt, chlorine, mineral or a fibreglass shell with a sensitive surface finish. It changes what we use and it is worth mentioning at quote stage.

This is the clearest case for anti slip sealing on a property

A sealed surround stops holding the moisture that grows the algae in the first place, and an anti slip additive in the coat adds measurable grip underfoot. On a travertine or honed bluestone surround used by children it is the single most worthwhile thing we can do to it. Anti slip sealing.

Questions

Asked about pool surrounds

Is the cleaning solution safe for my pool?

With the normal precautions, yes. Run off is directed away from the waterline, the skimmer is protected, and the chemistry is chosen so incidental overspray does not create a balance problem.

Tell us whether it is salt, chlorine or mineral when you book. It is the kind of detail that changes what we use.

My travertine has gone slippery. Can you fix it?

Cleaning removes the algal film, which is usually the whole problem and restores most of the grip immediately.

If the travertine is filled and has polished with wear, the grip issue is in the surface itself rather than on it, and that is where an anti slip sealer makes the genuine difference.

Can you clean the glass pool fence at the same time?

Yes, and it is worth doing together because the set up is shared. Pool glass marks differently from house windows: chlorinated splash dries repeatedly at the same height and leaves a dull band that ordinary washing does not shift.

Glass balustrade and pool glass covers it.

How often should a pool surround be cleaned?

Annually for most, heading into summer. A heavily shaded surround or one under trees can need it twice a year, because the damp conditions never really break.

The honest trigger is underfoot rather than visual. If it feels different barefoot and wet, it is due.

Will you damage the coping or the tiles?

Not at the pressures used on these surfaces. Travertine, bluestone and tiled coping are all cleaned at low pressure with the chemistry doing the work, and anything unusual gets a test patch first.

What does damage them is acid on travertine or limestone, which dissolves the surface permanently. We never use it on either.
